headlines.text: Food and drink: 4,735 new companies in the last 6 months, up 4.0% on the 6 months before and +10.5% on the year.
Craft makers (bakers, roasters, brewers, distillers): 184 new companies in the last 6 months, up 5.7% on the 6 months before and +14.4% on the year.
Creative and culture: 3,990 new companies in the last 6 months, down 6.4% on the 6 months before and +8.4% on the year.
Software and tech: 5,206 new companies in the last 6 months, up 15.7% on the 6 months before and +36.4% on the year.
WC1H is picking up fastest: 30 new companies in 6 months against 14 before.
DA6 is cooling fastest: 18 new companies in 6 months against 46 before.
The local mix is moving toward craft, creative, wellness and tech in SW7, E20, NW8: SW7's new companies are 68.2% in those sectors against 56.8% of what is there already.
New food and drink companies are registered most often in October (index 115, 100 = an average month) and least in December (88).
15.5% of food and drink companies formed 12 to 24 months ago are already being struck off or wound up, against 10.2% for creative and culture and 17.3% for independent retail.
Of 9,286 food and drink companies formed in the last year, 63.8% stand alone and 36.2% look linked to other food and drink companies (a shared name or address), a sign of groups and serial operators.
Matching 324 new premises to their companies: 56% belong to companies under a year old (new entrants) and 15% to companies over 3 years old (established operators adding a site or taking over).

method: Companies registered to a London postcode district in each sector, excluding mass-registration addresses. 'Linked' means a shared distinctive name stem or registered address with another food and drink company; the free file has no directors, so first-time founder is a likely, not a certain, label. Today's register is survivors, which slightly flatters the older half of any comparison. Premises are matched to companies by name within a postcode district, only when exactly one company fits.
